title: Microsoft Purview: DLP inline protection for more unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business
summary: Hold: the briefing gives Edge version 144 as the starting version, but the cited Microsoft Learn page now specifies version 158. The claim that automatically created security groups are read-only is also unsupported; the roadmap dates and published browser DLP licensing are supported.

claims.claim: Purview collection and DLP policies are planned to support browser inline protection for a significantly broader set of unmanaged generative AI apps in Edge for Business.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview collection and data loss prevention (DLP) policies will support browser inline protection for a significantly broader set of unmanaged generative AI apps in Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Administrators can use existing Purview policy experiences to detect and protect sensitive data shared through supported browser activities.
claims.quote: Admins can use existing Purview policy experiences to detect and protect sensitive data shared through supported browser activities, helping extend consistent data security controls across more destinations.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: previewDate; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap targets preview for January CY2027.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "January CY2027"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap targets general availability for February CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "February CY2027"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.quote: "targetDate": "February CY2027", "previewDate": "January CY2027", "moreInfoLink": null

claims.claim: Existing Edge for Business functionality enforces Purview DLP inline.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) monitoring and protection are built right into the Microsoft Edge for Business browser.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and devices
claims.claim: Browser policies targeting unmanaged apps apply on Windows 10 and Windows 11 desktop devices.
claims.quote: DLP policies that target unmanaged apps in the browser apply to Microsoft Edge for Business on Windows 10 and Windows 11 desktop devices managed by Microsoft Intune.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and devices
claims.claim: Policies targeting unmanaged apps use devices managed by Microsoft Intune.
claims.quote: You can use policies for unmanaged cloud apps in Edge for Business on Intune-managed devices

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and devices
claims.claim: Policies targeting unmanaged apps apply across all Edge browser profiles.
claims.quote: Policies targeting unmanaged apps on managed devices apply across all Edge browser profiles (work profile, personal profile and InPrivate).

claims.claim: The supported unmanaged apps include ChatGPT (consumer).
claims.quote:
Browser policies in Edge for Business support these unmanaged apps:
- Adobe Firefly
- CapCut
- ChatGPT (consumer)

claims.claim: The supported unmanaged apps include Google Gemini.
claims.quote:
- DeepSeek
- Google Gemini
- Grok (xAI)

claims.claim: The supported unmanaged apps include DeepSeek.
claims.quote:
- DeepAI
- DeepSeek
- Google Gemini

claims.claim: The supported unmanaged apps include Perplexity AI.
claims.quote:
- Otter.ai
- Perplexity AI
- QwenAI

claims.claim: Learn does not identify a separate expanded app set for this roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: '"571396" "Edge"' and 'Purview expanded unmanaged AI apps Edge 571396 default existing policies adaptive app scopes newly supported apps pricing'; read dlp-browser-dlp-learn and dlp-create-policy-block-to-ai-via-edge; neither maps its supported list to this roadmap expansion.

claims.claim: The printed Purview portal path reaches the All unmanaged AI apps scope for an inline DLP policy.
claims.quote:
Select + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes
Select All unmanaged AI apps > Add.
On the Choose where to enforce the policy step, select Edge for Business.
claims.fix: The printed path reaches app selection but omits the enforcement choice named in the control. Use 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes > All unmanaged AI apps > Choose where to enforce the policy > Edge for Business' in controls[0].ui.path and the rendered table.

claims.claim: Adaptive app scopes apply only to supported unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business.
claims.quote: Not all unmanaged AI apps are supported in Edge for Business. Adaptive app scopes apply only to the supported unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Saving the first applicable Purview collection or DLP policy automatically creates the required Edge configuration policies outside Purview.
claims.quote: After you save your first Purview collection or DLP policy targeting unmanaged apps in Edge for Business, the Microsoft Edge management service automatically creates the required Edge configuration policies, Microsoft Intune policies, and security groups

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: That first-policy activation automatically creates required Microsoft Intune policies.
claims.quote: the Microsoft Edge management service automatically creates the required Edge configuration policies, Microsoft Intune policies, and security groups needed to activate the policy in the browser and prevent circumvention.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Activation automatically creates two security groups.
claims.quote: 2 security groups are created — one for included users and one for excluded users — that match the scope of your Purview policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: A block policy prevents users in scope from using unprotected browsers where the policy does not apply.
claims.quote: If you configure the DLP policy to block, users in scope can't use unprotected browsers where the policy doesn't apply.

claims.claim: Policies can audit or block supported unmanaged-app upload activities.
claims.quote:
| Upload text | Managed | Unmanaged | allow, block, both actions audited |
| Upload file | Managed, Unmanaged | Managed, Unmanaged | allow, block, both actions audited |

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: This inline unmanaged-app control does not provide detection for apps outside its supported set.
claims.quote: Not all unmanaged AI apps are supported in Edge for Business. Adaptive app scopes apply only to the supported unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated how this expansion affects existing policies on arrival, so its default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Edge expanded unmanaged AI apps inline protection default rollout existing policies price meter 571396' and '"Purview" "All unmanaged AI apps" "automatically" "new"'; read the roadmap record, browser DLP Learn page, policy walkthrough and Edge activation page.

claims.claim: Detection uses destination-app traffic, which may differ from the originating app.
claims.quote: When you target an unmanaged cloud app in an Edge for Business browser policy, detection is based on the destination app's traffic, which isn't always exactly the same as the originating app.

claims.claim: Apps such as ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI may intermittently send encoded content that affects enforcement.
claims.quote: Some unmanaged AI apps like ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI might intermittently send content in encoded form or through dynamically generated endpoints, which can impact policy enforcement.

claims.claim: Those apps may use dynamically generated endpoints that affect enforcement.
claims.quote: Some unmanaged AI apps like ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI might intermittently send content in encoded form or through dynamically generated endpoints, which can impact policy enforcement.

claims.claim: Inline evaluation covers up to 4 MB for uploadText.
claims.quote: Inline evaluation size limits: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText, and files up to 3 MB for uploadFile.

claims.claim: Inline evaluation covers files up to 3 MB for uploadFile.
claims.quote: Inline evaluation size limits: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText, and files up to 3 MB for uploadFile.

claims.claim: Purview browser and network data security policies do not apply to B2B guest users.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview browser and network data security policies don't apply to B2B guest users.

claims.claim: A policy targeting an unmanaged app can capture consumer and enterprise interactions when their URL is shared.
claims.quote: Policies that target unmanaged apps can capture interactions from both the consumer and enterprise versions of an app when the app's URL is shared across instances (for example, ChatGPT consumer and ChatGPT enterprise).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Automatically created Edge configuration and Intune policies are read-only and updated through Purview policy changes.
claims.quote: Automatically created policies are read-only and are updated automatically by making updates to the policies in Purview.

claims.claim: The automatically created security groups are read-only.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "security groups" "read-only" "Edge"'; read microsoft-edge-dlp-purview-configuration, including How it works and FAQs. It calls policies read-only and groups automatically managed, but does not state that the security groups are read-only.
claims.fix: Replace 'the auto-created Edge configuration policies, Intune policies and security groups are read-only and are updated by editing the Purview policy' with 'the auto-created Edge configuration policies and Intune policies are read-only; these policies and the security groups update automatically when the Purview policy changes'. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-dlp-purview-configuration.

claims.claim: Automatically created policies and groups remain synchronized with changes to the Purview policies.
claims.quote: Once initially created, these policies and groups stay in sync and update automatically when changes are made to the Purview policies

claims.claim: Chrome may remain usable, with access to a set list of unmanaged generative AI apps blocked.
claims.quote: In Chrome browser: Use of the browser might be allowed depending on policy scope. If allowed, access to a set list of unmanaged generative AI apps is blocked.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users included in a blocking policy are prevented from using Firefox and other unprotected browsers.
claims.quote:
users included in Purview DLP policies that block data sharing to unmanaged cloud apps have their experience limited or blocked in unprotected browsers where the policies don't apply.
In Firefox and other browsers: Use of these browsers is blocked.

claims.claim: An automatic configuration sync failure prevents the unmanaged-app policies from being enforced in Edge for Business.
claims.quote: Purview doesn’t enforce DLP and collection policies for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business until you resolve the error.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An administrator with the required permissions must resync to resolve the automatic configuration failure.
claims.quote: An admin with the required permissions must resync to resolve the error.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Endpoint DLP policies take priority over browser inline DLP where user, context and action match.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP policies are prioritized over inline DLP policies for cloud apps in Edge for Business if the same user, context, and action are configured in both policies.

claims.claim: Browser inline DLP is included in the qualifying licences rather than separately metered in the cited service-description table.
claims.quote: | Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) inline data protection for data sharing to cloud apps in the browser. | Included | Included |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Office 365 E5/A5 also includes the browser inline DLP capability.
claims.quote:
| Office 365 E5/A5 |
| Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) inline data protection for data sharing to cloud apps in the browser. | Included | Included |

claims.claim: The browser DLP Learn page refers readers to Microsoft 365 plans and service descriptions for licensing.
claims.quote:
For information on licensing, see
- Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans
- Microsoft 365 Service Descriptions

claims.claim: No licensing change specific to this expanded app set is published in the checked Microsoft material.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "expanded" "unmanaged" "licensing"'; read the Purview service description browser DLP section and dlp-browser-dlp-learn licensing section. They state browser DLP entitlement but no licensing change specific to roadmap 571396.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A price or meter specific to this expanded app set is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Edge expanded unmanaged AI apps inline protection default rollout existing policies price meter 571396'; read the Purview service description browser/network DLP sections and the Learn billing-models search excerpt. No expansion-specific price or meter was stated.

claims.claim: The service description separately describes inline protection across the network as pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote:
## Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) for cloud apps accessed via the network
These features are pay-as-you-go capabilities.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; Scope: Roles; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Full activation requires Directory Reader permissions.
claims.quote:
To fully activate your Purview policies in Edge for Business, the admin needs these permissions:
- Directory Reader

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; Scope: Roles; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Full activation requires Microsoft Edge administration permissions.
claims.quote:
To fully activate your Purview policies in Edge for Business, the admin needs these permissions:

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; Scope: Roles; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Full activation requires Microsoft Intune administration permissions.
claims.quote:

claims.claim: Learn refers to its DLP deployment page for permissions to create and deploy DLP policies.
claims.quote: Permissions to create and deploy Microsoft Purview DLP policies are found here.

claims.claim: Learn lists these Edge for Business features as starting with version 144.
claims.quote: These features are available in the two latest stable versions of Edge for Business, starting with version 158.
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn lists Edge for Business versions from 144, in the two latest stable versions' with 'Learn lists these features as available in the two latest stable versions of Edge for Business, starting with version 158'. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-browser-dlp-learn#supported-browsers.

claims.claim: Learn specifies the two latest stable versions of Edge for Business.
claims.quote: These features are available in the two latest stable versions of Edge for Business, starting with version 158.

claims.where: Scope: Cloud and rollout; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Inline protection for unmanaged apps does not support tenants using Microsoft Intune multi-admin approval.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview inline protection in Microsoft Edge for Business for unmanaged apps doesn't support tenants that use multi-admin approval in Microsoft Intune.

claims.claim: The cited policy walkthrough initially runs the policy in simulation mode.
claims.quote: On the Policy mode page, select Run the policy in simulation mode.

claims.claim: All catalogue entries for a targeted app, such as QwenAI and Qwen Chat, should be included to avoid coverage gaps.
claims.quote: When multiple catalog entries exist for the same app with differences in the entry name (for example, QwenAI and Qwen Chat), include all entries for the app to avoid unintended coverage gaps.

claims.claim: The other-browser restriction does not affect users' experience in Edge for Business.
claims.quote: This restriction doesn't affect their experience in Microsoft Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Unmanaged-app activity can be reviewed in Activity explorer by filtering enforcement plane to browser.
claims.quote: You can view activities and audit log entries in activity explorer, audit logs, and Defender XDR investigations. In activity explorer, filter by enforcement plane set to browser.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Manual resync is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Edge > Monitoring > Microsoft Purview DLP protections > Sync now.
claims.quote:
Sign into the Microsoft Admin center
Navigate to Settings > Edge > Monitoring
On the Microsoft Purview DLP protections card, select Sync now

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or automation call for this Purview DLP configuration resync.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge Purview DLP protections Sync now resync API PowerShell security groups read only' and '"Purview" "Edge" "resync" "API"'; read microsoft-edge-dlp-purview-configuration. Results documented the admin-center Sync now action, not an API or cmdlet for it.

claims.claim: Resync does not create or update policies or groups when the administrator lacks their required permissions.
claims.quote: The resync action won't create or update the policies or groups where the Admin doesn't have the required permissions.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -EnforcementPlanes @("Browser") to create a policy with browser enforcement, not by itself its app scope or rule actions.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
The EnforcementPlanes parameter defines the layer where policy actions are run.
-EnforcementPlanes @("<Value>")
Browser: For use with policies applied to unmanaged cloud apps in Edge for Business.

claims.claim: The Learn policy-creation walkthrough uses a hypothetical scenario and values.
claims.quote: This article presents a hypothetical scenario with hypothetical values. It's only for illustrative purposes.

claims.claim: Automatic activation or configuration failure surfaces an error in Purview.
claims.quote: If automatic behaviors fail to create or update the policies or groups, an error message displays in Purview and policies aren't applied in Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Policy scope, rules and actions are configured in the Purview policy.
claims.quote:
Select Edit scope
On the Customize advanced DLP rules page, select + Create rule.
Under Actions, add an action with these values:

claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to check or take stock of is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote:
Check whether the tenant uses multi-admin approval in Microsoft Intune
Compare users in scope with any Endpoint DLP policies for the same actions
Review activity in Activity explorer
The table contains only inline policy scope/enforcement and configuration resync.
claims.fix: The Before rollout checks for Intune multi-admin approval and overlapping Endpoint DLP policies, and the After rollout Activity explorer review, have no corresponding controls-table rows. Do not add rows as part of this correction.
